title: SEO, AEO and GEO Audit: Checklist and What an Agency Should Deliver
excerpt: An SEO, AEO and GEO audit checklist for Indian businesses: what each audit checks, the evidence to ask for, acceptance checks and a fair agency brief.
intro: An SEO, AEO and GEO audit checks three things on the same website: whether search engines can crawl, index and rank your pages (SEO), whether those pages give clear, extractable answers to the questions buyers ask (AEO), and whether AI systems can identify, trust and cite your business accurately (GEO). A useful audit names each problem, shows the evidence, lists the affected URLs and says how the fix will be checked.

This guide gives you the checklist for all three and a brief you can hand to an agency or your own team. It is a practical worksheet for an Indian business, not a quotation, contract template or promise of a particular search result or AI citation. GrowwStack offers selected businesses individually agreed growth work; the scope and commercial arrangement require evaluation.

sections.heading: SEO, AEO and GEO audit checklist: what each audit checks
paragraphs: The three audits overlap, because answer engines and AI systems mostly reuse pages that are already crawlable and indexed. Google says its AI features need no special markup beyond normal Search eligibility, so the SEO layer comes first. Use the table to see what each layer adds and what evidence to ask for.

table.caption: What an SEO, AEO and GEO audit should check
head: Audit layer
What it checks
Evidence to ask for
rows: SEO: access and indexing
Robots rules, canonicals, noindex, sitemap, status codes, internal links to money pages
Search Console Pages report and URL Inspection results with dates
SEO: intent and pages
One owner page per search intent, titles and H1s that match the query, duplicate or thin pages
Query-to-page map from Search Console, with impressions and average position
SEO: performance and mobile
Core Web Vitals, mobile layout, render-blocking scripts
PageSpeed Insights or field data for named URLs
AEO: answer quality
A direct 40-70 word answer under the heading, clear H2 questions, tables or steps where the topic suits them
List of buyer questions and the URL that answers each one
AEO: structured data
FAQPage, Article, Product or Organization markup that matches visible content
Rich Results Test or Search Console Enhancements report
GEO: entity and facts
One consistent fact set (name, what you do, where, founder) across the site, profiles and directories
A table of the facts as they appear on each source, with mismatches marked
GEO: AI crawler access and citations
Bot access for search and AI crawlers, and whether AI answers cite or describe you correctly
Dated prompt checks per engine, separating a mention, a citation and a referred visit

list: Important pages return 200, are canonical to themselves and are not blocked or noindexed.
Each important query has one owner page; no two pages compete for the same term.
Each owner page answers its main question in the first paragraph.
Structured data parses and matches what a reader sees on the page.
Business facts are identical on the site, in profiles and in directory listings.
Reports use fixed date ranges, a fixed query cohort and separate brand from non-brand.
Every fix has an acceptance check and a date on which it will be reviewed.

sections.heading: Write the business problem in one paragraph
paragraphs: State who you sell to, what you sell, where you can serve customers and what a useful enquiry or purchase looks like. Add the current constraint: no relevant discovery, weak enquiry quality, poor product information or unreliable follow-up. These problems need different work even when all are described as needing SEO.

For a hypothetical industrial supplier, the brief might ask for serviceable RFQs containing a product family and intended application. For a D2C store, it might ask for discovery of available categories with reliable order tracking. These are examples of scope, not target results or client outcomes.

sections.heading: Specify the baseline and access before the recommendations
paragraphs: Request a business-owned Search Console property and analytics view with defined reporting windows. The supplier should record filters, countries, devices and data availability. Share the minimum authorized access needed for the work, rather than moving ownership of the domain or analytics account to the supplier.

Ask for a fixed cohort of relevant queries, page-level opportunities and separate brand/non-brand interpretation. Average position is not a fixed ranking. Missing query rows are not rank zero. An audit that reports only green percentage changes without counts and date ranges makes it difficult to assess progress.

sections.heading: Require a page-level issue register
paragraphs: A useful row contains the affected URL, the observed issue, evidence date, business consequence, recommended change, dependency, owner and acceptance check. A statement such as improve technical SEO is too broad to assign or verify. A specific canonical mismatch or broken internal link is actionable when the evidence supports it.

Group issues into access/indexing, information quality, site navigation, performance and measurement. Keep verified defects separate from experiments. For example, a failed form save is a defect; testing a clearer page title is an optimization hypothesis. They should not receive the same confidence label or review process.

sections.heading: Make AEO and GEO deliverables inspectable
paragraphs: Ask which buyer questions the work will answer and which pages will answer them. Require the factual reviewer, source requirements and publication checks. If the proposal includes AI visibility monitoring, define platforms, prompts, geography where observable, capture dates and the difference between a mention, a citation and a referred visit.

For Google AI features, the official guidance does not require special AI markup. That does not make content quality or technical access optional. Treat llms.txt as supplementary experimentation rather than a deliverable that establishes placement. The [AEO guide](/blog/answer-engine-optimization-aeo) and [GEO guide](/blog/generative-engine-optimization-geo) explain the boundaries.

If you are comparing providers for this work, the [AEO and GEO services guide](/blog/aeo-geo-services-india) lists the deliverables to expect, and [GrowwStack's SEO services](/services) shows how the audit feeds an ongoing programme.

sections.heading: Use acceptance checks instead of a blog quota
paragraphs: An article is complete when the intended reader can use it, the facts are reviewed, the page is live and the technical checks pass. It is not complete merely because a document was written. Ask which existing page would be improved instead if a proposed topic duplicates its intent.
list: Named primary intent and destination URL, checked against existing content.
Original useful answer with accurate claims and clear illustrative examples.
Descriptive metadata, appropriate canonical and accessible internal links.
Valid structured data matching visible content, where appropriate.
Rendered mobile review, working next step and live deployment evidence.
Sitemap/indexing status recorded without promising inclusion.

sections.heading: Compare scope, costs and ownership together
paragraphs: Ask which work is included, what depends on your team and what is billed separately. A fixed retainer, deferred project payment and revenue share are different arrangements. A headline such as pay after results does not identify the payment trigger or define the underlying result.

Record content and account ownership, the review cadence and the handover process in the proposal discussion. Use the [SEO payment-model guide](/blog/pay-after-results-seo-india) to compare outcome definitions and the [retainer versus revenue-share comparison](/blog/marketing-retainer-vs-revenue-share-cost) to frame costs. Neither replaces review of your actual agreement.

sections.heading: Ask for a report that can show failure
paragraphs: Require the same tracked cohort and comparable complete periods even when visibility declines. Show what shipped, what was verified live, what indexing state is actually known and what remains blocked. Keep enquiries and sales separate from search clicks. An honest report can say that work is complete but its effect cannot yet be measured.

Use a first pilot to test the working relationship: one bounded business problem, a small set of relevant pages and explicit checks. Review whether the supplier explains uncertainty and changes course when evidence disagrees. A proposal becomes useful when the business can tell what happened without relying on a ranking guarantee.

faqHeading: SEO, AEO and GEO audit: common questions

faq.q: What is the difference between an SEO audit, an AEO audit and a GEO audit?
faq.a: An SEO audit checks whether search engines can crawl, index and rank your pages. An AEO audit checks whether those pages give clear answers that can be shown as snippets or in AI answers. A GEO audit checks whether AI systems can identify your business and describe it correctly, which depends on consistent facts across your site and other sources.

faq.q: Do I need a separate AEO or GEO audit if I already have an SEO audit?
faq.a: Usually not a separate project. Google says its AI features use the same Search eligibility as normal results, so the SEO checks come first. AEO and GEO add checks on answer quality, structured data and entity facts; a good audit covers all three in one issue register.

faq.q: How long should an SEO, AEO and GEO audit take?
faq.a: It depends on the number of pages and the access you can give. For a small business site, the useful output is a page-level issue list with evidence and acceptance checks, not a long PDF. Ask the provider to state the time and the access they need before they start.

faq.q: Can an audit guarantee that ChatGPT or Google's AI Overviews will cite my business?
faq.a: No. No provider controls which sources an AI system cites. An audit can remove technical barriers, improve answers and fix inconsistent facts, and it can measure citations with dated prompt checks, but it should never promise placement.

faq.q: What should I share with an agency for the audit?
faq.a: Read access to your own Search Console property and analytics, the list of products or services that matter most, and examples of good enquiries or orders. Keep ownership of the domain and accounts with your business and give only the access the work needs.
